awarding_body.value: Board of Certification for Emergency Nursing (BCEN)

year_launched.note: BCEN was established in 1980 ('Est. 1980' per BCEN logo/footer) and CEN is its founding, longest-running credential. Exact first CEN administration year not stated verbatim on a single fetched page; year reflects BCEN founding.

eligibility.value: Current, unencumbered Registered Nurse (RN) license in the United States, a U.S. Territory, Canada, or Australia. A foreign nursing certificate equivalent to a U.S. RN license is also acceptable (verified through TruMerit). No clinical-setting requirement. Any active restriction, suspension, or probation on a nursing license disqualifies a candidate.

experience_recommendation.value: BCEN recommends at least two years of experience in the specialty area before scheduling, but this is not required.

exam_format.value: Computer-based at Pearson VUE test centers; also offered via Live Remote Proctoring. 175 total questions (150 scored, 25 unscored pretest). Time limit 3 hours.

passing_score.note: BCEN uses a scaled passing score set by a criterion-referenced standard-setting study; the exact raw scored-item cut score for CEN is not published as a fixed number on the fetched pages. Marked null rather than guessed.

fee_military.note: Active-duty, reservist, and veteran rate on initial, retest, and recertification applications

fee_test_assurance_nonmember.note: Initial exam with optional Test Assurance (second attempt if first is unsuccessful)

renewal.value: CEN is valid for four years. Renew via Recertification by CE Attestation (100 contact hours within the 4-year period; at least 75 hours of clinical content specific to the specialty, up to 25 may be non-clinical; at least 50 hours from an accredited provider such as BCEN Learn, AACN, ANCC, ENA, ABA, STN, or ASTNA) OR via Recertification by Examination.

common_confusions.value: CEN (board certification, ED breadth) vs. TCRN (BCEN trauma-continuum certification), CPEN (BCEN pediatric ED), CFRN (BCEN flight transport), and TNCC/ENPC (ENA provider courses, not certifications).

salary_context.value: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics OEWS (May 2024) reports a mean annual wage of about $98,430 for registered nurses; emergency-department RNs and certified nurses frequently command pay above the median.

recent_changes.value: BCEN published an updated CEN Examination Content Outline effective July 6, 2026, expanding to 11 subject areas: Gastrointestinal becomes its own section (split from GI/GU/Gyn/OB), Maxillofacial and Ocular is renamed Head, Eye, Ear, Nose, Throat Emergencies, and Professional Issues is reorganized into Prioritization (triage, mass casualty, throughput) and Legal/ethical issues. The exam stays 175 items / 150 scored / 3 hours.

blueprint.note: Sum of Musculoskeletal and Wound (13) + Maxillofacial and Ocular (11).

blueprint_note: Official 01-2022 CEN Content Outline scored-item counts (sum to 150): Cardiovascular 19, Respiratory 18, Neurological 18, GI/GU/Gyn/OB 18, Mental Health 11, Medical 14, Musculoskeletal & Wound 13, Maxillofacial & Ocular 11, Environment/Toxicology & Communicable Diseases 14, Professional Issues 14. The data file uses the canonical 10-domain split with raw scored-item counts to avoid double-counting. New 11-area outline effective 2026-07-06.

pass_rate_history.note: Pass rate = exams passed / (passed + failed) = 4198 / 8172 = 51.4%. Using delivered as denominator yields 47%. Reported figures are BCEN ABSNC-mandated statistics for Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2025.

discrepancies: Question count: certs.js lists CEN at 175 items, which matches BCEN (175 total / 150 scored). No conflict.

Pass rate denominator: BCEN reports 8,889 exams delivered but 4,198 passed + 3,974 failed = 8,172. The 717-exam gap (no-shows/incomplete) means pass rate is 51% on completed exams or 47% on delivered. Page uses 51% (completed) and footnotes the basis.
